authority.principle: Facts follow evidence. Design decisions stop for the human operator.

library.access: read-only unless the batch is explicitly library work

canonicalClaudeMdSections.note: These CLAUDE.md sections are declared canonical by name rather than copied. CLAUDE.md is digest-checked by the contract, so a change to any of them invalidates the contract.
sections: Where truth lives (precedence: code > Storybook render > production behaviour > Figma)

agentRules.lead: Any agent — Claude, Codex, or other — editing the Figma files or this repo follows the same loop. Work that skips it gets audited and may be superseded.

rules.title: Read before touching
rules.text: Read before touching: CLAUDE.md, then use the validated compact workflow for NPVE work (run node scripts/workflow/validate-workflow.js, read workflow/npve-contract.generated.json, the selected manifest item, and its last record). For other workstreams, or when the compact workflow routes you there, read design-system-schema.json. The schema remains the authoritative record; the generated contract is a freshness-checked projection; chat history and your own memory are not the record.
rules.note: Amended 2026-09-08 (commit c88ce6c) to route NPVE work through the compact workflow; that amendment had no record until workflowRefactor_closeout_2026-09-08.

rules.title: Audit before building
rules.text: Audit before building: when the current state is uncertain, run a read-only inventory first and report it. Never build onto an unverified state.

rules.title: One batch at a time
rules.text: One batch at a time, with a stop condition stated up front. A batch that grows past its stop condition becomes two batches.

rules.title: Additive only
rules.text: Additive only. Nothing is deleted, and nothing is moved, renamed, or superseded without a record saying so. Archives get a README.

rules.title: No invention
rules.text: No invention. If the library and code lack a pattern, mark it (GAP/DEFECT per the convention) and build with what exists. Recreating a source drawing by hand and calling it a component is a false record, which is worse than the gap.

rules.title: Verify in pixels
rules.text: Verify in pixels. Screenshot what you built and look at it. Property readbacks are claims; renders are evidence. After editing a component, re-screenshot its live instances and diff.

rules.title: Record every batch
rules.text: Record every batch: a dated schema record via an apply-*.js script, backup first, findings to flags[]. A batch without a record did not happen and will be treated as suspect.

rules.title: Report per rule 13
rules.text: Report per rule 13: full report to disk, short reply, no tables in chat. Change logs in the file are written in plain graphic-design language, not system jargon.

rules.title: Stop on disagreement
rules.text: When sources disagree or a decision is needed, stop and report. Precedence (code > Storybook render > library > source) resolves facts, not design decisions.

rules.title: Record gate
rules.text: Record gate. Before starting any batch, check that the previous batch in this workstream has a schema record. If it does not, refuse the batch and run a read-only state check instead; its record stands in for the missing one.

rules.title: Risk is planner/operator-owned
rules.text: Risk is planner/operator-owned, never executor-owned. Classes are low, medium, high and human-decision as defined in workflow/protocol.json. A manifest tier counts as approved only when the operator's approval is quoted verbatim in the manifest and the record; an unapproved tier lets an item proceed only with per-item operator confirmation, also quoted; a human-decision item does not start until the operator decides. Deterministic gates may compress checks, but every component still gets a comparison render inspected by the executor and shown to the operator.
rules.note: Adopted from amendment 2 of the 2026-09-08 plan review; first written into AGENTS.md by commit c88ce6c as its rule 10, which made AGENTS.md diverge from CLAUDE.md. Numbered 11 in both files from this record on.

recordGate.text: Before starting any batch, check that the previous batch in this workstream has a schema record. If it does not, refuse the batch and run a read-only state check instead; its record stands in for the missing one. In the compact workflow the gate is enforced twice: the apply-*.js script refuses to create the IN PROGRESS record while the previous record is not DONE, and start-batch.js refuses to start while the item's own record is not IN PROGRESS or a dependency is not complete.

14.title: Change log beside every rebuilt frame
14.text: Every rebuilt frame has a Change log beside it, on its right, listing what changed from the source, from → to, and why in one line, in plain graphic-design language. Rows come from the batch prompt. The change log lives once, as a `_Rebuild comparison/Change log/<screen>` sub-component on Templates holding Change log/Row instances; Row stays a component so styling propagates. The schema remains the record; the change log is its plain-language view.
14.note: Added 2026-09-02; amended the same day to the detached-frame convention (flag npveChangelog_placedLogIsDetached); rewritten 2026-09-04 in repair batch 2 to the instance-swap sub-component convention that stands today.

15.title: Rebuild comparison is the only placement
15.text: Every rebuilt frame sits in a Rebuild comparison on Screens: an instance of the Rebuild comparison master whose three content slots are swapped per screen to `_Rebuild comparison/Reference|Rebuild|Change log/<screen>` sub-components, left to right on a grey backdrop. Each screen and its change log exist exactly once, inside those sub-components; the comparison instance is the only placement, and a fix goes to the sub-component, never to a copy. The reference is a flat export at 2x captioned with its source node id and export date, and does not update when the source changes. The grey backdrop is a deliberate exception to rule 10.
15.note: The 2x reference is produced with the Figma MCP download_assets (source node, png, scale 2) and placed with upload_assets targeting the reference rectangle (method recorded in npveRebuild_comparisonLayout_2026_09_02.transport). Verification proofs are not placements; see proofConvention.

items: Sheets are as tall as their content. The Sidesheet master stays 550 by 600. A placed sheet grows or shrinks to fit its body, and the footer sits right under the last row. Never pad a short sheet to 600 or pin its footer to the bottom.

Helpers under a short sheet are transparent. When a rebuilt sheet is shorter than the comparison slot, the Rebuild sub-component carries no fill, so only the sheet shows white. Nothing false extends below it.

Tall content overflows the slot; the slot does not shrink it. When a reference or a rebuilt sheet is taller than the 600 slot, keep it at 1:1 and switch clipping off on that column of the placed comparison instance. Never scale a reference to fit.
New bodies join the shell through its Body content list. Append the new body component to the Sidesheet's Body content preferred values and leave the default alone. Do not fork the shell.
A new state is a new variant of the body it belongs to. Add State=Empty to the existing body set rather than creating a second set or a loose frame.

Values the library lacks may live in a local NPVE collection. Name the collection NPVE/<kind>, record the operator's decision in the schema, claim no code syntax, and add the value to the library to-do list. Never write it into the library from a consuming file.

proofConvention.text: Verification proofs — instances or frames placed only so a batch can read rendered paint and property state — are named `PROOF — <batch folder> · <what>`, live only through their batch, and are archived under additive-only at batch close: moved unchanged to the Archive page section `06 · Pilot proofs`, listed in the Archive README, never deleted. A proof is not a placement under rule 15 and is never fixed in place; fixes go to the master or sub-component.

operatingLoop: Validate this contract before reading it as current truth.
Record gate: confirm the previous batch in the workstream has a schema record; if not, refuse and run a read-only state check whose record stands in.
Use the manifest item selected by the planner; the executor may not change its risk class. An unapproved tier needs per-item operator confirmation, quoted verbatim.
Verify file identity and current live state before writes.
Declare one bounded batch and stop condition.
Create the IN PROGRESS schema record before Figma mutation, regenerate this contract, then start the batch guard.
Mutate sequentially; stop on the first component failure before touching the next item.
Run deterministic checks and inspect at least one comparison render per component.
Save the comparison render and full report; show the render to the operator.
Archive the batch proofs per proofConvention, finalize the schema record, regenerate this contract, pass the finish gate, and commit with an explicit allowlist.

standingBatchRules._purpose: Non-negotiable checks every future batch runs before reporting. Added after the paint-opacity defect reached four already-signed-off components.
standingBatchRules.1_instancePaintVerification: Place ONE INSTANCE of every new variant and read its RENDERED paints — colour, effective alpha and bound variable — comparing each against its master. Master-level reads are NOT evidence: paint-level opacity renders correctly on a master and incorrectly on an instance, which is exactly how the defect survived four batches. Any alpha must live in the variable's stored rgba, never as paint-level opacity. SCOPE: that last sentence governs UNBOUND paints only - for a BOUND paint Figma surfaces the variable's stored alpha into paint.opacity, and that mirrored value is correct; read rule 9_boundPaintAlpha before touching it.
standingBatchRules.2_unboundPaintAudit: Walk EVERY top-level node on EVERY page, not just component sets. Reference frames, notes frames and loose glyphs count. Auditing only component sets is what let 3 unbound paints sit in the Radio reference frame across several batches.
standingBatchRules.3_referenceCounts: Count componentPropertyReferences per variant after any clone or combineAsVariants — cloning a variant inside a set silently drops them all.
standingBatchRules.4_skipInvisibleFalse: Set figma.skipInvisibleInstanceChildren = false before any audit walk, so boolean-hidden slots are inspected.
standingBatchRules.5_opacityLast: If paint-level opacity is genuinely unavoidable somewhere, apply it as the final operation AND verify on an instance. Prefer promoting to a computed variable.
standingBatchRules.6_enumerateDontRecall: When remediating or sweeping, enumerate from the file rather than from a previously reported list. The alpha remediation's known list was missing 18 of 48 paints.
standingBatchRules.7_fileIdentityFirst: Every Figma call passes fileKey YX2n4YLrEpBXNbcc73T6dw explicitly — never rely on an ambient or last-used file. Every session's FIRST Figma action verifies file identity against this schema's page inventory (figmaBuild.pages._order) before any read informs a decision or any write occurs; if the page list does not match, stop and report rather than proceeding. Added 2026-08-03 after a session read the legacy team library (ZPf0sJy83aPyrHjCVHomya, 'Tebra Working UI Kit') and produced a full reorganisation analysis against the wrong file. Note that figma.root.name returns 'Document' for both files, so the file NAME is not a usable identity check — the page list is.
standingBatchRules.8_roundWithRecord: Never carry a fractional dimension into Figma. Two cases, one treatment. (a) pxToRem inflation, where an intended integer exists behind the fraction: bind the intended integer, record computedPx. (b) Authored-fractional sources, where no intended integer exists — a fractional spacing multiplier, a viewBox ratio, a non-square viewBox in a square box: ROUND to the nearest integer and record the true value as computedPx in both the component description and the schema, and label the rounding a design decision with its source and date. Added 2026-08-03 when the primary nav produced the first case-(b) values (76.8, 44.8, 23.88, 18.24); Daniel ruled round-with-record as design authority. Intrinsic geometry is out of scope for this rule: VECTOR and GROUP bounds are the union of their path data, are not authored, and are not rounded — the tier 6 illustrations already set that precedent.
standingBatchRules.9_boundPaintAlpha: Before changing ANY paint-level opacity, first check whether that paint has a bound colour variable. If it does, Figma SURFACES the variable's stored alpha into paint.opacity - it does NOT multiply the two. A paint bound to a variable storing rgba(0,0,0,0.87) correctly reads back paint.opacity 0.87 and renders at 0.87; that is the expected state, not a double-alpha defect, and it must be left alone. Forcing such a paint to opacity 1 DISCARDS the alpha and renders the node fully opaque. Rule 1's 'never as paint-level opacity' applies to UNBOUND paints only. Established empirically 2026-08-26 (checkboxFlushHaloFix2026_08_26d.alphaFindingThatOverturnsAnEarlierEntry) after the opposite assumption produced a real regression on Alert filled/warning; reverted and audited library-wide 2026-08-27 (boundAlphaRegressionRevert2026_08_27). To re-confirm at any time: bind a rectangle to an alpha-carrying variable, never set opacity, then read paint.opacity back - it returns the variable's alpha.
standingBatchRules.10_cloneDropsPropertyRefs: Cloning a variant to add a new axis value DROPS componentPropertyReferences on every child. The clone keeps its layers and looks correct, but Label/icon-visibility/icon-swap stop responding — instance property values are stored yet never render, so a swapped instance silently shows the component default. After any variant clone, re-apply refs by copying them from a known-good sibling keyed on child layer name, then verify by reading a nested instance rendered characters against its property value, not just the property value. Hit during buttonInheritColour2026_08_28.
